design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomly allocated to the treatment or control group using complete randomization in SPSS.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated using SPSS, but there is no information on allocation concealment until assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 64 participants were randomized (conducted with complete randomization using SPSS package for Windows, version 17.0) to atorvastatin treatment group (n = 32) or control group (n = 32).

domain_judgments.rationale: This was an open-label, non-placebo-controlled study where participants and trial personnel were aware of treatment assignments, and analyses were conducted only on completers (n=30 per group) rather than a strict intention-to-treat framework.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The treatment group received 10 mg/day atorvastatin and lifestyle guidance, while the control group received lifestyle guidance only. ... non-placebo-controlled design

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data were minimal and balanced across groups (2 out of 32 dropouts in each arm, >93% retention) with clear non-differential reasons provided.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After 1-year follow-up, 60 subjects completed the treatment with atorvastatin or control, respectively (Fig. 1). In the former, two patients were lost to follow-up at weeks 4 and 24, respectively. In the latter, two drop-outs occurred at weeks 4 and 24, respectively.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were bone mineral density measured by DXA and automated biochemical immunoassays, which are objective measurements unlikely to be influenced by lack of blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: BMD of hip and lumbar spine was measured with dual-energy X-ray absorptionmetry (DXA). ... Serum CTx, OC and 25(OH)D were measured by automated immunoassay analyzers

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-trial registration or published statistical analysis plan was mentioned, introducing some concerns regarding selective outcome reporting or multiple analysis choices.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary endpoint: comparison of BMD at total hip, lumbar spine and femoral neck between atorvastatin and control groups from baseline to month 12.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to an unspecified method of allocation concealment, an open-label design analyzed on completers only, and lack of trial pre-registration.

design_rationale: The study is described as a double-blind clinical trial where eligible participants were randomly divided into blocks containing 4 people in each one.

domain_judgments.rationale: While the text mentions permuted block randomization of size 4, it also confusingly states that 'sequential nonrandom sampling method was used', with no details provided regarding allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: People qualified for the research were randomly divided into randomized blocks containing 4 people in each one... Sequential nonrandom sampling method was used in both groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although described as double-blind, vitamin B1 pills may differ in appearance, taste, or odor from atorvastatin tablets, potentially compromising blinding, and no adherence or ITT details are provided.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients and the measurers had no idea of the variables associated with attribution of the patients... 40 mg atorvastatin pills... was used in the case group while 100 mg pills of B1 vitamin produced by Darou Pakhsh Co. was used as placebo for witness group

domain_judgments.rationale: All 20 patients in each group appear to have completed the 6-week trial and had outcome data analyzed with no dropouts reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The case group included 20 patients suffering from PCOS who received atorvastatin, while there were 20 patients with PCOS in the witness group who just received placebo... All the variables were studied once again after 6 weeks and the results were analyzed using SPSS v.16.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory and Doppler ultrasound measurements, and outcome assessors were reported to be blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients and the measurers had no idea of the variables associated with attribution of the patients... Vaginal Doppler and sonography were carried out by radiologist in sonography ward of Firouzgar Hospital.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-specified statistical analysis protocol was reported to confirm that outcomes and analyses were not selected post hoc.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All the variables were studied once again after 6 weeks and the results were analyzed using SPSS v.16.

overall_summary: The trial has some concerns overall due to unclear allocation concealment alongside contradictory statements regarding sampling, potential unblinding from the use of commercial vitamin B1 as a placebo, and the absence of a pre-registered protocol.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to atorvastatin or placebo using a computer-generated randomization list.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was computer-generated and concealed using numbered containers labeled by independent personnel, with balanced baseline characteristics between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Forty subjects who fulfilled both inclusion and exclusion criteria were randomly assigned to the atorvastatin or the placebo group based on a computer-generated randomization list. Each randomization number corresponded with one of the two possible interventions, and labeling was done by personnel not involved in the trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind design with placebo prevented awareness of assigned intervention, and the small number of early noncompliant dropouts (3 of 40) is unlikely to bias the estimated effect of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study was undertaken using atorvastatin 20 mg daily... Thirty-seven patients completed the study. Two patients from the placebo group... and one patient from atorvastatin group... dropped out of the study within 4 wk due to noncompliance.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data were very low (3/40, 7.5%), balanced between groups (1 vs 2), with reasons clearly documented and unlikely to depend on true outcome values.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thirty-seven patients completed the study. Two patients from the placebo group (patient 10, age 27, body mass index (BMI) 32.9, and patient 14, age 26, BMI 33.4) and one patient from atorvastatin group (patient 37, age 26, BMI 32.9) dropped out of the study within 4 wk due to noncompliance.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective automated laboratory assays measured in a double-blind trial, precluding measurement bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Serum testosterone was measured on an Architect analyzer (Abbott Laboratories, Maidenhead, UK) and SHBG by an immunometric assay with fluorescence detection on the DPC Immulite 2000 analyzer using the manufacturer’s recommended protocol.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was prospectively registered and all pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints were fully analyzed and reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint of the study was a change in hsCRP, and the secondary endpoints were a change in homeostasis model assessment for insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) and total testosterone... This study was registered in the International Standard Randomized Controlled Trial Number (ISRCTN) registry as ISRCTN24474824.

overall_summary: The study is a well-conducted double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial with low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains. Randomization, blinding, objective outcome assessment, and complete reporting of pre-specified outcomes were properly executed.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to atorvastatin or placebo using a computer-generated randomization list in blocks of 6.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was randomly generated, concealed using sequentially numbered envelopes by pharmacy staff not involved in the study, and baseline differences were consistent with chance in a small sample.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was conducted using a computer-generated randomization list in blocks of 6, and it was carried out at the Oulu University Hospital Pharmacy by personnel not involved in the study. They also repacked the medication in closed envelopes, which were sequentially numbered.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although double-blinding was maintained with matching placebo, 10 of 38 randomized participants were excluded post-randomization and a complete-case/per-protocol analysis was conducted rather than intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the first 4 months of the study, 4 women (2 subjects in the atorvastatin group and 2 in the placebo group) were excluded as a result of nonadherence to the study protocol, 1 subject from the placebo group withdrew because of myalgia, and 1 from the atorvastatin group withdrew because of arthralgia. Twentyeight women completed the study (n = 15 in the atorvastatin group; n = 13 in the placebo group) and were included in the analysis

domain_judgments.rationale: Over 26% of randomized participants (10 of 38) were excluded or lost post-randomization without intention-to-treat analysis or imputation, which could plausibly bias the outcome estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 38 Caucasian women with PCOS... participated in the study... Twentyeight women completed the study (n = 15 in the atorvastatin group; n = 13 in the placebo group) and were included in the analysis (Figure 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory and metabolic test measurements assessed using standardized, validated biochemical assays with blinding maintained.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Serum samples for testosterone were analyzed by using Agilent triple-quadrupole 6410 liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry equipment... Concentrations of insulin, C-peptide, LH, and FSH were analyzed by using an automated chemiluminescence system... All samples (ie, baseline and 3 and 6 months) from the same subject were analyzed in the same assay.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively and reported outcomes match the predefined primary and secondary measures and standard analytic approaches.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was registered at the Clinical Trials Register (identifier code NCT01072097; http://clinicaltrials.gov) and EU Clinical Trials Register (identifier code 2006-003584-31; https://www. clinicaltrialsregister.eu).

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall due to missing outcome data and per-protocol analysis excluding over 26% of randomized participants, despite sound randomization, blinding, and objective outcome measurement.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to atorvastatin or placebo using a permuted block randomization scheme generated by a biostatistician.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated using permuted blocks by a biostatistician and administered by an independent pharmacist via over-encapsulation, ensuring concealment, and baseline characteristics were comparable.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The biostatistician generated a permuted block randomization scheme for the allocation sequence and provided it to the pharmacist. The atorvastatin and placebo were over-encapsulated by the pharmacist so that the participants, research coordinator who administered the intervention, and investigators who assessed the outcomes were blinded to group assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, research coordinators, and investigators were blinded via identical over-encapsulated capsules, and an intention-to-treat analysis using linear mixed-effects models was planned and executed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The atorvastatin and placebo were over-encapsulated by the pharmacist so that the participants, research coordinator who administered the intervention, and investigators who assessed the outcomes were blinded to group assignment... All analyses were performed by intention-to-treat using SAS software, version 9.1

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 2 of 20 randomized participants did not complete treatment (10%), linear mixed-effects models were used which accommodate missing values under MAR, and the small amount of missingness is unlikely to bias the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Twenty eligible women were randomized and started the allocated treatment. Eighteen women completed their treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were blinded to group assignment, and objective physiological and laboratory measurements were used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The atorvastatin and placebo were over-encapsulated by the pharmacist so that the participants, research coordinator who administered the intervention, and investigators who assessed the outcomes were blinded to group assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: No clinical trial registry number or pre-published statistical analysis plan was cited, and the trial was terminated early after an interim-like look at the data when 20 participants completed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Recruitment was slow due to strict inclusion/ exclusion criteria so we analyzed our data after the first 20 women completed the study. This analysis revealed that the required sample size was 235 subjects per group for 80% power to detect an absolute 2% increase in FMD with Atorvastatin compared to Placebo... We stopped the trial early because we had insufficient funds for the required sample size.

overall_summary: The study was a well-blinded randomized placebo-controlled trial, but carries some concerns regarding selection of the reported result due to lack of an explicit pre-registered protocol and early trial cessation after an unplanned look at the data following recruitment of 20 participants.
